project.name: experimental-FRC
project.description: An FRC (FIRST Robotics Competition) robot codebase for Team 4935, built on WPILib/GradleRIO (2026.2.1) with CTRE Phoenix 6, AdvantageKit, PathPlannerLib, and the maple-sim physics simulator, following a hardware-isolation architecture that keeps IO interfaces separate from subsystem logic. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: FieldConstants.java
nodes.summary: Holds field-wide geometry constants (AprilTag field layout, field dimensions) and computes the alliance-relative middle starting pose used for autonomous setup.

nodes.name: FieldConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder class for the AprilTag field layout, field dimensions, and alliance-mirrored middle starting poses.

nodes.name: middleStartFor
nodes.summary: Returns the correct middle-starting Pose2d for the given DriverStation alliance color.

nodes.name: OperatorControls.java
nodes.summary: Binds driver joystick, operator control-box, and simulated-controller inputs to drivetrain teleop drive, target-tracking, POI auto-align, and Superstructure shoot/intake/eject commands.

nodes.name: OperatorControls
nodes.summary: Owns the driver joystick, operator control box, and sim controller instances and wires them to drivetrain/Superstructure commands.

nodes.name: configureBindings
nodes.summary: Registers all button/axis bindings for driving, hub/pass target tracking, POI auto-align, and shoot/intake/eject commands, for both real and simulated controllers.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Publishes raw joystick axis values to SmartDashboard each loop for driver-station telemetry.

nodes.name: POI.java
nodes.summary: Defines named field Points of Interest with alliance-mirrored poses and rotations, used by the drivetrain's driveToPOI auto-align command.

nodes.name: POI
nodes.summary: Enumerates field Points of Interest, storing blue/red poses and rotations and exposing alliance-resolved accessors.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Resolves this POI's Pose2d for the currently detected DriverStation alliance, defaulting to blue.

nodes.name: getTargetRotation
nodes.summary: Resolves this POI's target Rotation2d for the currently detected alliance, defaulting to blue.

nodes.name: CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java
nodes.summary: CTRE Tuner X generated swerve drivetrain subsystem, extended with SysId routines, PathPlanner autonomous integration, vision-fused pose estimation, and target-tracking/POI auto-align driving commands; also owns the simulation thread wiring to MapleSim.
nodes.languageNotes: Sanctioned CTRE hardware-isolation exception per project architecture rules — this file legitimately contains vendor (Phoenix 6/CTRE) APIs directly, unlike standard subsystem files.

nodes.name: CommandSwerveDrivetrain
nodes.summary: Generated CTRE swerve drivetrain subsystem extended with SysId characterization, PathPlanner autonomous configuration, vision pose fusion, and custom auto-align/target-tracking drive commands.

nodes.name: setSysIdRoutine
nodes.summary: Selects which SysId characterization routine (translation/steer/rotation) is currently active for testing.

nodes.name: useTranslationSysId
nodes.summary: Convenience helper that switches the active SysId routine to translation characterization.

nodes.name: useSteerSysId
nodes.summary: Convenience helper that switches the active SysId routine to steer characterization.

nodes.name: useRotationSysId
nodes.summary: Convenience helper that switches the active SysId routine to rotation characterization.

nodes.name: CommandSwerveDrivetrain
nodes.summary: Constructor overloads that build the swerve drivetrain from generated TunerConstants, regulate module constants for simulation, log CANcoder boot readings, start the sim thread, and configure the PathPlanner auto-builder.

nodes.name: logCancoderBootReadings
nodes.summary: Waits for all CANcoder status signals at boot and logs each module's absolute encoder reading and health status for calibration verification.

nodes.name: configureAutoBuilder
nodes.summary: Configures PathPlanner's AutoBuilder with robot-relative speed control, PID constants, and alliance-based path flipping, and logs active/target path telemetry.

nodes.name: applyRequest
nodes.summary: Returns a Command that continuously applies a supplied SwerveRequest to the drivetrain.

nodes.name: sysIdQuasistatic
nodes.summary: Runs the currently selected SysId routine's quasistatic characterization test in the given direction.

nodes.name: sysIdDynamic
nodes.summary: Runs the currently selected SysId routine's dynamic characterization test in the given direction.

nodes.name: driveToPOI
nodes.summary: Builds a FunctionalCommand that closed-loop drives the robot to a given POI's pose using independent X/Y/rotation PID controllers, finishing within tolerance.

nodes.name: trackHub
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper around trackTarget that continuously aims the drivetrain heading at the vision-estimated hub position.

nodes.name: trackPassTarget
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper around trackTarget that continuously aims the drivetrain heading at the vision-estimated pass target.

nodes.name: trackTarget
nodes.summary: Generic heading-lock driving command that PID-controls rotation toward a supplied target position while a driver supplies translational input.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Per-loop update that applies operator perspective based on alliance, seeds pose from the field-relative middle start on the first disable-to-enable transition, and logs drivetrain telemetry.

nodes.name: startSimThread
nodes.summary: Spins up the MapleSimSwerveDrivetrain physics model and a periodic Notifier thread that updates the simulated drivetrain each sim loop.

nodes.name: resetPose
nodes.summary: Resets both the estimated pose and, in simulation, the MapleSim world pose to keep them synchronized.

nodes.name: getMapleSimDrive
nodes.summary: Exposes the underlying MapleSim drivetrain simulation object for external simulation queries.

nodes.name: getSimulatedGroundTruthPose
nodes.summary: Returns the physics-simulated ground-truth pose of the drivetrain, distinct from the estimated pose, for simulation validation.

nodes.name: getRawGyroYawDegrees
nodes.summary: Returns the raw Pigeon2 gyro yaw reading in degrees, bypassing pose estimation.

nodes.name: addVisionMeasurement
nodes.summary: Overloaded vision-measurement ingestion methods that feed timestamped camera pose estimates, with optional custom standard deviations, into the drivetrain's pose estimator.

nodes.name: samplePoseAt
nodes.summary: Samples the historical pose estimate at a given timestamp, correcting for FPGA time offset.

nodes.name: Vision.java
nodes.summary: Singleton vision subsystem that estimates hub/pass target positions and headings from AprilTag geometry, fuses camera pose estimates into the drivetrain odometry, and computes shooter RPM from a distance lookup table.

nodes.name: Vision
nodes.summary: Singleton subsystem managing AprilTag-based vision: hub/pass target geometry, IMU-assist mode switching, pose fusion into the drivetrain estimator, and shooter RPM interpolation.

nodes.name: getInstance
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the Vision singleton, choosing VisionIOReal or VisionIOSim based on runtime mode.

nodes.name: getHubPosition
nodes.summary: Computes the alliance-correct hub AprilTag translation from the field layout, falling back to empty if the tag pose is unavailable.

nodes.name: getHubHeading
nodes.summary: Derives the robot-relative heading to the hub from the current pose and the hub position.

nodes.name: getPassTargetPosition
nodes.summary: Averages the alliance's pass-target AprilTag positions into a single passing target translation.

nodes.name: getPassHeading
nodes.summary: Derives the robot-relative heading to the pass target from the current pose.

nodes.name: getPoseResetEstimate
nodes.summary: Delegates to the vision IO layer for a one-shot pose estimate usable to reset drivetrain odometry.

nodes.name: setIMUMode
nodes.summary: Forwards an IMU fusion mode change (e.g. SEED to FUSION) to the vision IO layer and tracks the current mode locally.

nodes.name: getIMUMode
nodes.summary: Returns the currently active IMU assist mode.

nodes.name: setIMUAssistAlpha
nodes.summary: Forwards an IMU-assist blending alpha value to the vision IO layer and tracks it locally.

nodes.name: hubDistanceMeters
nodes.summary: Computes the straight-line distance from the current (or vision) pose to the hub position, if both are known.

nodes.name: calculateRPM
nodes.summary: Converts hub distance into a target shooter RPM via the RPM lookup table, clamped to a safe range.

nodes.name: interpolateRPM
nodes.summary: Linearly interpolates target RPM between the two nearest calibrated distance/RPM lookup-table entries.

nodes.name: fuseMeasurements
nodes.summary: Filters and fuses camera pose measurements against the current estimate, rejecting large jumps and computing distance-scaled standard deviations before feeding the drivetrain's pose estimator.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Per-loop update that feeds gyro yaw into the vision IO, processes AdvantageKit inputs, fuses pose measurements, and publishes hub/pass distance and RPM telemetry.

nodes.name: MapleSimSwerveDrivetrain.java
nodes.summary: Wraps the MapleSim physics simulation library to model swerve module drive/steer motors and gyro behavior in simulation, used by CommandSwerveDrivetrain's sim thread.

nodes.name: MapleSimSwerveDrivetrain
nodes.summary: Bridges CTRE's generated swerve drivetrain to the MapleSim physics simulation, wiring simulated drive/steer motor controllers and gyro state.

nodes.name: MapleSimSwerveDrivetrain
nodes.summary: Constructs the MapleSim drivetrain simulation from robot mass/bumper/motor/COF parameters and module locations, wiring per-module simulated drive and steer motor controllers.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Advances the simulated arena physics and pushes the simulated pose/rotation and angular velocity into the Pigeon2 gyro simulation state.

nodes.name: regulateModuleConstantsForSimulation
nodes.summary: Applies simulation-safe overrides to every swerve module's constants before the drivetrain is constructed.

nodes.name: regulateModuleConstantForSimulation
nodes.summary: Overrides a single module's encoder offset, inversion flags, and steer gains/friction/inertia with simulation-appropriate defaults when not running on real hardware.

nodes.name: RobotLifecycleTest.java
nodes.summary: JUnit lifecycle test that boots Robot on a background thread under HAL simulation and verifies Vision's IMU mode transitions from SEED to FUSION on entering autonomous.

nodes.name: RobotLifecycleTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test fixture that boots a real Robot instance on a background thread under WPILib HAL simulation for lifecycle testing.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: Initializes the HAL, resets DriverStation simulation data, pauses sim timing, and starts the Robot main loop on a daemon thread before the test runs.

nodes.name: teardown
nodes.summary: Ends competition mode, joins the robot thread, asserts it exited cleanly, and closes Robot resources after each test.

nodes.name: autonomousInitSwitchesIMUModeFromSeedToFusion
nodes.summary: Enables autonomous mode via DriverStationSim and asserts that Vision's IMU mode transitions from SEED to FUSION as a result.

nodes.name: RobotContainer.java
nodes.summary: Wires together the robot's singleton subsystems (drivetrain, intake, shooter, vision, superstructure) at startup, registers PathPlanner auto commands, and binds driver/operator/sysid controls.

nodes.name: RobotContainer
nodes.summary: Central composition root holding subsystem singletons and building the auto chooser, control bindings, and sysid routines for the whole robot.

nodes.name: RobotContainer
nodes.summary: Constructs the robot, registers PathPlanner NamedCommands (homing, orbit, shooting sequences, intake start/stop) that route through Superstructure's state machine, then builds the auto chooser and control bindings.

nodes.name: dashboard
nodes.summary: Publishes Shooter telemetry and state-machine-respecting SmartDashboard buttons (Intake/Eject/Stow/Shoot) that funnel through Superstructure instead of raw subsystem commands.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Forwards the scheduler's periodic tick to OperatorControls so driver/operator dashboard values stay current.

nodes.name: configureBindings
nodes.summary: Binds drivetrain idle-while-disabled behavior and sysid quasistatic/dynamic triggers on the sysid controller, then delegates driver/operator button bindings to OperatorControls.

nodes.name: getAutonomousCommand
nodes.summary: Returns the currently selected autonomous routine from the SmartDashboard auto chooser.

nodes.name: TunerConstants.java
nodes.summary: CTRE Tuner X-generated swerve drivetrain constants (module gear ratios, PID/feedforward gains, CAN IDs, module offsets/positions) and the factory for constructing CommandSwerveDrivetrain.
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-generated by CTRE's Tuner X Swerve Project Generator; contains direct Phoenix 6 vendor API usage (TalonFXConfiguration, CANcoderConfiguration, Pigeon2Configuration) that would normally violate the project's hardware-isolation rule outside *IOReal files, but this file is machine-generated tuner output and is the sanctioned exception feeding CommandSwerveDrivetrain.

nodes.name: TunerConstants
nodes.summary: Holds all four swerve module hardware configurations (drive/steer motor IDs, CANcoder offsets, module positions) plus shared gains and CAN bus config generated by CTRE's Tuner X tool.

nodes.name: createDrivetrain
nodes.summary: Factory method that instantiates CommandSwerveDrivetrain with the four generated SwerveModuleConstants and drivetrain-wide constants.

nodes.name: Intake.java
nodes.summary: Singleton Intake subsystem controlling the roller and pivot mechanism, with mechanism-level jam detection and an automatic eject-pulse recovery routine built into setRoller().

nodes.name: Intake
nodes.summary: SubsystemBase singleton exposing roller control (with jam recovery), pivot positioning, homing, and roller SysId routines; backed by an IntakeIO implementation selected per Constants.currentMode.
nodes.languageNotes: Jam recovery (detect stall via stator current + low velocity, then pulse EJECT for a fixed duration followed by a cooldown before re-arming) lives entirely inside setRoller() so every caller -- teleop, autos, Superstructure -- gets stall protection for free, per the project's intake jam-recovery migration.

nodes.name: getInstance
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the Intake singleton, selecting IntakeIOReal or IntakeIOSim based on Constants.currentMode.

nodes.name: Intake
nodes.summary: Builds the roller SysIdRoutine (voltage ramp/step, motor log callback) and initializes the "Intake/Zeroed" dashboard flag.

nodes.name: setRoller
nodes.summary: Applies a roller state, but for INTAKE requests first checks isJammed() and -- if stalled and not already recovering/cooling down -- drives a timed EJECT pulse followed by a cooldown before resuming INTAKE, encapsulating jam recovery at the mechanism level.

nodes.name: getRollerState
nodes.summary: Returns the roller state most recently commanded via setRoller().

nodes.name: rollerSysIdQuasistatic
nodes.summary: Runs the roller's quasistatic SysId characterization and stops the roller when finished.

nodes.name: rollerSysIdDynamic
nodes.summary: Runs the roller's dynamic SysId characterization and stops the roller when finished.

nodes.name: goTo
nodes.summary: Commands the pivot to a named PivotState angle via the IO layer.

nodes.name: goToDegrees
nodes.summary: Commands the pivot to an arbitrary angle in degrees, bypassing the named PivotState enum.

nodes.name: agitatePivot
nodes.summary: Repeatedly cycles the pivot between AGITATE and DOWN while running the roller inward, used to shake loose jammed fuel; owned/scheduled by Superstructure's ensureAgitating().

nodes.name: eject
nodes.summary: Command that reverses the roller while held and stops it on release.

nodes.name: startRoller
nodes.summary: Command that runs the roller inward while held and stops it on release.

nodes.name: hardstop
nodes.summary: Returns true when pivot stator current exceeds the hardstop threshold, signaling the pivot has hit its mechanical limit during homing.

nodes.name: homing
nodes.summary: Drives the pivot toward its hardstop at a fixed voltage, zeroes the encoder once the hardstop is detected (or after a 1s timeout), then returns to the DOWN position.

nodes.name: stopRoller
nodes.summary: One-shot command that stops the roller.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Updates IO inputs (optionally overridden by test-only jam simulation fields), logs them via AdvantageKit, and publishes stall/pivot-angle telemetry to SmartDashboard.

nodes.name: IntakeIOSim.java
nodes.summary: WPILib-physics-only IntakeIO implementation (SingleJointedArmSim pivot + DCMotorSim roller) with no vendor hardware dependencies, plus maple-sim IntakeSimulation integration for game-piece pickup.
nodes.languageNotes: Confirms both pivot and roller motors as Kraken X60 per the mentor-verified hardware pass; lazily wires an IntakeSimulation to RobotContainer.drivetrain's maple-sim drivetrain the first time updateInputs() runs, once the drive sim is available.

nodes.name: IntakeIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulated intake IO backing pivot position/voltage control and roller velocity/voltage control with closed-loop PD/P math run manually each cycle, plus fuel pickup simulation.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Steps the pivot and roller physics sims each cycle (applying closed-loop voltage from local PD/P control when active), zeroes outputs while disabled, lazily creates the maple-sim IntakeSimulation once the drivetrain sim is available, and starts/stops fuel intake based on roller state.

nodes.name: setPivotVoltage
nodes.summary: Applies a clamped open-loop voltage to the simulated pivot and disables its closed-loop position hold.

nodes.name: setPivotPosition
nodes.summary: Sets a closed-loop position setpoint for the simulated pivot.

nodes.name: setPivotEncoderPosition
nodes.summary: No-op in simulation since the physics model already tracks true pivot position directly, unlike real hardware which needs an encoder re-zero.

nodes.name: setRollerVoltage
nodes.summary: Applies a clamped open-loop voltage to the simulated roller and marks intake simulation as not running.

nodes.name: setRollerVelocity
nodes.summary: Sets a closed-loop velocity setpoint for the simulated roller and marks intake simulation running when velocity is positive.

nodes.name: Shooter.java
nodes.summary: Singleton Shooter subsystem controlling flywheel RPM, agitator, and indexer motors, with a jam-clearing indexJam() routine and Shuffleboard-tunable RPM via initSendable().

nodes.name: Shooter
nodes.summary: SubsystemBase singleton exposing flywheel spin-up/RPM control, agitator and indexer voltage control, and Shuffleboard-driven RPM tuning; backed by ShooterIOReal/ShooterIOSim per Constants.currentMode.

nodes.name: getInstance
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the Shooter singleton, selecting ShooterIOReal or ShooterIOSim based on Constants.currentMode.

nodes.name: setAgitator
nodes.summary: Applies an Agitate enum voltage to the agitator motor and records the current state for telemetry.

nodes.name: getAgitateState
nodes.summary: Returns the agitator state most recently commanded via setAgitator().

nodes.name: agitate
nodes.summary: Command that drives the agitator inward while held and stops it on release.

nodes.name: agitateReverse
nodes.summary: Command that drives the agitator outward while held and stops it on release.

nodes.name: agitateStop
nodes.summary: Repeating command that continuously commands the agitator to stop.

nodes.name: indexJam
nodes.summary: Sequenced jam-clearing routine for the indexer: index until isJammed() trips, then repeatedly pulse EJECT/INDEX to clear the stall.

nodes.name: setRPMShooter
nodes.summary: Commands the flywheel to a closed-loop RPM setpoint via the IO layer.

nodes.name: targetRPMShooter
nodes.summary: Sets the desired flywheel target RPM field and applies it via setRPMShooter().

nodes.name: getTargetRPM
nodes.summary: Returns the currently targeted flywheel RPM.

nodes.name: setOutputShooter
nodes.summary: Drives the flywheel with an open-loop voltage percentage instead of closed-loop RPM.

nodes.name: stopShooter
nodes.summary: Commands the flywheel target RPM to zero.

nodes.name: spin
nodes.summary: Command that sets the target RPM then waits until the flywheel reaches speed within tolerance.

nodes.name: dashSpin
nodes.summary: Deferred command wrapper around spin() using the live targetRPM field, for dashboard-driven tuning.

nodes.name: shooterAtSpeed
nodes.summary: Returns true when the current flywheel velocity is within tolerance of the given target RPM.

nodes.name: indexControl
nodes.summary: Applies an indexing enum voltage to the indexer motor and records the current state for telemetry.

nodes.name: getIndexerState
nodes.summary: Returns the indexer state most recently commanded via indexControl().

nodes.name: index
nodes.summary: Command that drives the indexer forward while held and stops it on release.

nodes.name: indexEject
nodes.summary: Command that drives the indexer in reverse while held and stops it on release.

nodes.name: initSendable
nodes.summary: Publishes flywheel RPM, target RPM, and tuning-mode fields to Shuffleboard/SendableBuilder for live dashboard tuning.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Updates and logs ShooterIO inputs each cycle, and when tuning mode is enabled, drives the flywheel from the dashboard-tunable target RPM/voltage.

nodes.name: Superstructure.java
nodes.summary: Singleton Superstructure implementing the project's centralized 254-style state machine (OFF/INTAKING/EJECTING/STOWED/ALIGNING/SHOOTING) that arbitrates Shooter, Intake, and Vision directly from periodic(), per architecture rule 3.
nodes.languageNotes: Arbitration logic lives entirely in periodic()'s switch-case rather than in composed Commands; shootCmd()/shootingSequence() are documented in-source as thin Command bridges kept only because RobotContainer's whileTrue binding and PathPlanner's NamedCommands require real Command objects.

nodes.name: Superstructure
nodes.summary: SubsystemBase singleton owning Shooter/Intake/Vision references and the SuperstructureState machine that decides each tick's actual state and commands subsystems accordingly.

nodes.name: getInstance
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs the Superstructure singleton given a drivetrain reference (needed to obtain Vision).

nodes.name: requestShoot
nodes.summary: Requests the shooting sequence -- the no-arg overload holds indefinitely for teleop hold-to-shoot, while the timeoutSeconds overload uses bounded align/settle/feed windows for autonomous use.

nodes.name: requestIntake
nodes.summary: Requests the INTAKING wanted state for active floor intake.

nodes.name: requestEject
nodes.summary: Requests the EJECTING wanted state to reverse intake roller and indexer for unjamming/dumping.

nodes.name: requestStow
nodes.summary: Requests the STOWED wanted state and clears the in-progress shot flag.

nodes.name: getSystemState
nodes.summary: Returns the current actual SuperstructureState.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Transitions mSystemState, resetting the state-entry timestamp and cancelling the agitate command when leaving ALIGNING/SHOOTING.

nodes.name: updateShooterRPM
nodes.summary: Drives the flywheel target RPM either from the dashboard tuning value or from Vision's calculated firing-solution RPM.

nodes.name: shootCmd
nodes.summary: Thin Command bridge that requests SHOOTING on start and STOWED on end/release, kept for RobotContainer's whileTrue teleop binding.

nodes.name: intakeCmd
nodes.summary: Thin Command bridge for hold-to-intake: requests INTAKING on start and STOWED on release.

nodes.name: ejectCmd
nodes.summary: Thin Command bridge for hold-to-eject: requests EJECTING on start and STOWED on release.

nodes.name: stowCmd
nodes.summary: Self-finishing command that requests STOWED once.

nodes.name: shootingSequence
nodes.summary: Thin Command bridge for autonomous/NamedCommands use: requests a bounded-timeout shoot and waits until the shot completes.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: The state machine's core: advances mSystemState from the wanted state (except mid-ALIGNING/SHOOTING), then commands Shooter/Intake per the current state in a switch-case covering OFF/STOWED/INTAKING/EJECTING/ALIGNING/SHOOTING.

nodes.name: SuperstructureEjectingTest.java
nodes.summary: JUnit HIL-style simulation test verifying that Superstructure.ejectCmd() drives the intake roller/indexer/agitator into their EJECTING outputs, and that cancelling it returns everything to STOWED (roller stopped).
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately kept to a single @Test method in its own class because build.gradle forks a fresh JVM per test class (forkEvery = 1), and the Superstructure/Intake/Shooter singletons have no reset hook -- a second method here would observe state left behind by the first.

nodes.name: SuperstructureEjectingTest
nodes.summary: Test fixture that boots a real Robot on a background thread under paused SimHooks timing, then drives/steps it to exercise Superstructure's EJECTING state end-to-end.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: Initializes HAL, resets DriverStationSim, pauses sim timing, and starts a Robot instance on a daemon thread, waiting for competition-loop startup.

nodes.name: teardown
nodes.summary: Ends the robot competition loop, joins its thread with a 1s timeout, asserts it exited, closes the robot, and resumes sim timing.

nodes.name: ejectCmdDrivesEjectingThenCancelStopsRoller
nodes.summary: Enables the robot in teleop, schedules Superstructure.ejectCmd(), asserts the intake roller/indexer/agitator reach their EJECTING outputs, then cancels the command and asserts the roller returns to STOP.

nodes.name: Constants.java
nodes.summary: Robot-wide static constants: CAN IDs for intake/shooter motors, vision camera names and standard-deviation tuning, and placeholder physical/simulation constants (masses, MOIs, reductions, bumper footprint) most of which are marked TODO pending real-robot measurement.
nodes.languageNotes: Flat public-static-final field holder plus a nested Mode enum (REAL/SIM/REPLAY) driven by RobotBase.isReal() -- the standard AdvantageKit-style mode-select pattern; no logic beyond field declarations.

nodes.name: Constants
nodes.summary: Final utility class holding every robot-wide numeric/boolean constant (motor CAN IDs, vision tuning, intake/shooter/agitator physical and simulation parameters) plus the REAL/SIM/REPLAY Mode enum used to select the active IO layer.

nodes.name: IntakeIOReal.java
nodes.summary: IntakeIO implementation for real TalonFX hardware -- configures Motion Magic position control for the pivot and velocity control for the roller, and is the only intake file permitted to touch CTRE Phoenix 6 APIs per the hardware-isolation rule.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CTRE Phoenix 6's fluent *Configuration builder pattern (withMotorOutput/withCurrentLimits/withMotionMagic/withSlot0) applied via getConfigurator().apply(cfg).

nodes.name: IntakeIOReal
nodes.summary: Real-hardware IntakeIO implementation wrapping two TalonFX motors (pivot, roller); configures Motion Magic/PID gains and current limits on construction and exposes voltage/position/velocity setters plus telemetry readback via updateInputs.

nodes.name: configurePivot
nodes.summary: Builds and applies the TalonFXConfiguration for the intake pivot motor: brake mode, sensor-to-mechanism reduction from Constants, 70/120A current limits, and Motion Magic cruise velocity/acceleration with PD+kV Slot0 gains.

nodes.name: configureRoller
nodes.summary: Builds and applies the TalonFXConfiguration for the intake roller motor: coast mode, velocity PID/kV Slot0 gains, and 90/120A current limits.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Reads TalonFX telemetry (connected state, position, velocity, applied voltage, stator/supply current, temperature) for both pivot and roller motors into the shared IntakeIOInputs struct.

nodes.name: ShooterIOReal.java
nodes.summary: ShooterIO implementation for real TalonFX/TalonFXS hardware -- configures velocity-torque-FOC control for the shoot flywheel, voltage control for the indexer, and a NEO 550-on-TalonFXS agitator; the only shooter file permitted to touch CTRE Phoenix 6 APIs.
nodes.languageNotes: The shoot Slot0 uses an intentionally extreme kA (50) relative to kV (0.215), documented in-line as a real build constraint: one Kraken X60 drives all 4 flywheels (high reflected inertia) on an underhand shot.

nodes.name: ShooterIOReal
nodes.summary: Real-hardware ShooterIO implementation wrapping the shoot (TalonFX), index (TalonFX), and agitator (TalonFXS/NEO 550) motors; configures PID/current-limit gains on construction and exposes voltage/velocity setters plus telemetry readback via updateInputs.

nodes.name: configureShoot
nodes.summary: Builds and applies the TalonFXConfiguration for the shoot flywheel motor: coast mode, 80/120A current limits, and Slot0 PID/kA/kV gains tuned for the high-inertia 4-flywheel underhand shot mechanism.

nodes.name: configureIndex
nodes.summary: Builds and applies the TalonFXConfiguration for the indexer motor: coast mode and 70/120A current limits.

nodes.name: configureAgitator
nodes.summary: Builds and applies the TalonFXSConfiguration for the NEO 550 agitator motor: coast mode, 80/120A current limits, and NEO550_JST motor-arrangement/commutation config confirming the Talon FXS drives a brushed NEO 550.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Reads TalonFX/TalonFXS telemetry (connected state, position, velocity, applied voltage, stator/supply current, temperature) for the shoot, index, and agitator motors into the shared ShooterIOInputs struct.

nodes.name: ShooterIOSim.java
nodes.summary: ShooterIO implementation backed by WPILib physics simulation (FlywheelSim for the shoot motor, DCMotorSim for index and agitator) with no vendor hardware dependencies, used for desktop/sim-only testing and replay.
nodes.languageNotes: Confirms real hardware identity in comments: shoot/index are Kraken X60 (DCMotor.getKrakenX60), agitator is a NEO 550 (DCMotor.getNeo550) driven through a TalonFXS, matching ShooterIOReal's MotorArrangementValue.NEO550_JST configuration.

nodes.name: ShooterIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulation ShooterIO implementation driving a FlywheelSim (shoot) and two DCMotorSims (index, agitator) built from Constants MOI/reduction values, with closed-loop velocity control for the shoot flywheel and open-loop voltage for index/agitator.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Advances the shoot/index/agitator physics sims by one loop period, applying closed-loop velocity control (with a simple kP term) to the shoot flywheel when enabled, and writes resulting position/velocity/current readings into ShooterIOInputs.

nodes.name: Robot.java
nodes.summary: WPILib/AdvantageKit robot entry point (extends LoggedRobot) that wires up logging receivers per REAL/SIM/REPLAY mode, owns RobotContainer and the Vision/HubActiveState singletons, and drives the command scheduler and vision IMU-mode transitions across the mode lifecycle.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the AdvantageKit pattern of switching data receivers/replay source on Constants.currentMode (REAL/SIM/REPLAY) inside the constructor, a common WPILib logging-framework idiom.

nodes.name: Robot
nodes.summary: Top-level TimedRobot/LoggedRobot subclass implementing all mode-lifecycle callbacks (init/periodic per mode) and holding references to RobotContainer, HubActiveState, and Vision.

nodes.name: robotPeriodic
nodes.summary: Runs every 20ms regardless of mode: drives HubActiveState and RobotContainer periodics, publishes match time to SmartDashboard, and runs the CommandScheduler.

nodes.name: autonomousInit
nodes.summary: Switches vision IMU mode to fused mode (4) with a low assist alpha at the start of autonomous and schedules the RobotContainer's chosen autonomous command; comment documents a prior odometry-snap bug from staying in EXTERNAL_SEED mode too long.

nodes.name: teleopInit
nodes.summary: Transitions vision to fused IMU mode at teleop start, cancels any running autonomous command, and applies a pending pose-reset estimate from Vision to the drivetrain if present.

nodes.name: HubActiveState.java
nodes.summary: Singleton utility that tracks whether the team's scoring hub is active during a match, computing time-segment-based active/inactive windows for teleop based on which alliance won auto, and publishing the result to NetworkTables with AdvantageKit replay support.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps its replayable state (isHubActive, timeUntilTransition) in a HootReplayBridge so AdvantageKit auto-replay can restore these fields without touching DriverStation APIs directly during replay.

nodes.name: HubActiveState
nodes.summary: Singleton (private constructor + static getInstance()) that determines hub-active windows during teleop from time segments keyed on which alliance won autonomous, and republishes state to NetworkTables each periodic call.

nodes.name: updateStatesForTeleop
nodes.summary: Determines hub active/inactive state and time-until-transition during teleop by checking the current match time against precomputed winner/loser time segments, selected via an XOR of which alliance won auto and which alliance we're on.

nodes.name: fetchInputs
nodes.summary: Dispatches hub-active-state computation based on current DriverStation mode: forces inactive when disabled, forces active during autonomous, and delegates to updateStatesForTeleop() during teleop.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Fetches fresh inputs when not replaying (letting AdvantageKit auto-replay fill in state otherwise), then publishes hub-active and time-until-swap values to NetworkTables.

nodes.name: IntakeJamRecoveryTest.java
nodes.summary: JUnit integration test that boots a real Robot on a background thread and drives INTAKING through Superstructure to verify that Intake's jam-recovery pulse fires on a forced jam, auto-resumes INTAKE after the pulse and cooldown, and aborts cleanly on a mid-pulse requestStow().
nodes.languageNotes: Runs robot.startCompetition() in a real background Thread with SimHooks.pauseTiming()/stepTiming() to deterministically advance a real command-scheduler loop instead of mocking Robot, matching the same harness pattern used by sibling RobotLifecycleTest/SuperstructureEjectingTest.

nodes.name: IntakeJamRecoveryTest
nodes.summary: Package-private test class (deliberately in frc.robot.subsystems.intake for access to Intake's test-only jam hooks) with setup/teardown lifecycle and a single end-to-end jam-recovery test method.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: JUnit @BeforeEach that initializes HAL, resets DriverStationSim data, pauses sim timing, constructs a real Robot on a daemon thread, and waits for startCompetition() to reach steady state.

nodes.name: teardown
nodes.summary: JUnit @AfterEach that ends competition, joins the robot thread with a 1s timeout asserting it exited, closes the robot, and resumes sim timing.

nodes.name: jamTriggersRecoveryPulseThenResumesAndAbortsOnStop
nodes.summary: End-to-end test driving Superstructure.requestIntake(), forcing a jam condition twice to verify the recovery pulse (EJECT) fires and auto-clears back to INTAKE after cooldown, then confirms a mid-pulse requestStow() immediately aborts the pulse to STOP.

nodes.name: main.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that builds and tests the robot code on every push or pull request to any branch, running inside the WPILib roboRIO cross-compilation Docker container.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs on ubuntu-22.04 inside the wpilib/roborio-cross-ubuntu:2025-22.04 container to match the FRC roboRIO toolchain; the single 'build' job checks out the repo, marks it as a safe git directory, grants gradlew execute permission, then runs `./gradlew build`, which compiles and runs tests in one step.

nodes.name: PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Draft plan (2026-07-17) for closing the evidence gap in gate 3 of the Advanced Agent Verification Loop: adds a sim-mode WPILOGWriter, logs the Limelight IMU mode to AdvantageKit outputs, and adds JUnit sim tests to prove the MegaTag2 IMUMode(4) fix and Superstructure EJECTING behavior from real log bytes. Plan-only document, no code changed yet.

nodes.name: claude.md
nodes.summary: Project-level Claude agent guidelines for the FRC 4935 hybrid refactor: defines architecture rules (hardware IO isolation, singleton subsystems, centralized Superstructure state machine), the Karpathy anti-failure-mode protocol, build/test/gate commands, the Obsidian vault sync workflow, and current task state (next-up items, backlog, and an unresolved prompt-injection watch tied to upstream issue #75758).

nodes.name: architecture.md
nodes.summary: Rationale layer behind CLAUDE.md's Architecture Rules, recording why each of the three enforced rules (hardware isolation, singleton subsystems, centralized Superstructure state) exists, the sanctioned CommandSwerveDrivetrain vendor exception, an accepted scheduler-requirements gap, and a reference-pattern adoption queue sourced from 254/1678/6328.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion doc to CLAUDE.md — CLAUDE.md holds the enforceable rule statements while this file holds the why, decided edges, and accepted gaps; updated only when a session revises an architecture decision.

nodes.name: history.md
nodes.summary: Append-only, oldest-first changelog of every completed refactor and verification pass on the codebase (Intake/Shooter/Vision IO isolation, Superstructure state-machine build-out, JUnit behavior tests, and seven logged prompt-injection attempts), moved out of CLAUDE.md so that file stays a current-state snapshot.
nodes.languageNotes: Doubles as a security incident log: records seven distinct <system-reminder> injection attempts across four sessions asking the agent to silently accept false file-state claims, plus the cross-reference to upstream GitHub issue anthropics/claude-code#75758.

nodes.name: verification-loop.md
nodes.summary: Defines the mandatory three-gate (plus 2.5) verification lifecycle behind CLAUDE.md's Verification Loop mandate — static compile, headless sim launch, JUnit behavior tests, and WPILOG evidence parsing — along with non-negotiable honesty rules banning canned/hardcoded verification output.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinguishes what a headless-sim PASS proves (construction/boot) from what it does not (command or state-machine behavior), which is why gate 2.5 (./gradlew test) exists as a separate, stricter gate.

nodes.name: 2026-07-16-maple-sim-physics.md

nodes.name: 2026-07-16-vision-superstructure-cleanup.md

nodes.name: 2026-07-17-intake-jam-recovery-migration-plan.md

nodes.name: 2026-07-17-phase3-imu-mode-junit-test.md
nodes.summary: Phase 3 test plan proving the IMUMode 1-to-4 autonomous transition in simulation: scaffolds a RobotLifecycleTest boot proof and forkEvery harness, extends it to the autonomous transition, parses the resulting .wpilog as an evidence gate, and wires ./gradlew test into the Verification Loop as gate 2.5.

nodes.name: 2026-07-17-phase3-test-b-ejecting-junit-test.md

nodes.name: 2026-07-16-maple-sim-physics-design.md
nodes.summary: Approved Phase 3 design spec for replacing the drivetrain's physics-free WPILib sim loop with maple-sim rigid-body physics, adding a MapleSimSwerveDrivetrain helper, and wiring IntakeIOSim to a real simulated game-piece-contact signal (2026 'Fuel' game piece).
nodes.languageNotes: Structured as five numbered implementation sections plus Context/Out-of-scope/Verification, each citing exact file paths and public API surfaces to be added — a spec-as-contract style rather than narrative prose.

nodes.name: 2026-07-16-vision-superstructure-cleanup-design.md
nodes.summary: Approved design spec consolidating command/helper sprawl ahead of Phase 3: folds PoseHelpers and RoboMath into Vision, replaces Intake_Start/Intake_Stop with Intake command factories, pulls Superstructure.java forward to host shootCmd()/shootingSequence(), and moves AutoAlignPOI/Target logic into CommandSwerveDrivetrain.
nodes.languageNotes: Each section pairs a 'Problem' statement with a 'Change' section containing literal proposed Java code and an explicit list of consumers to rewire, and ends with files slated for deletion — a clear before/after refactor contract.

nodes.name: 2026-07-17-intake-jam-recovery-migration-design.md
nodes.summary: Approved design spec moving jam detection/recovery from the legacy intakeJamReverse() Command into a mechanism-level interception point inside Intake.setRoller(), fixing an agitator-direction bug and a 'two writers, same tick' Superstructure bug, and migrating NamedCommands to route through Superstructure with an accompanying jam-recovery unit test.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents a mid-implementation revision (the test harness switching from direct Intake.setRoller() calls to routing through Superstructure.requestIntake()/requestStow()) discovered because a first approach failed deterministically — a rare case of a design doc recording its own correction.

nodes.name: parse_akit_log.py

nodes.languageNotes: Implements the WPILib Data Log File Format Spec v1.0 by hand (varint/string4 decoding, control records) rather than depending on an external log-reading library.

nodes.name: parse_log
nodes.summary: Walks the raw WPILOG byte buffer record-by-record, tracking start/finish/set-metadata control records to build a table of active log entries and append decoded records to each.

nodes.name: decode_scalar
nodes.summary: Decodes a single WPILOG record payload into a Python value based on its declared type string (boolean, int64, float, double, string, or array variants).

nodes.name: pose_jump_analysis
nodes.summary: Decodes an entry's pose2d records and flags consecutive samples whose translation delta exceeds a distance threshold, surfacing odometry/pose-estimator discontinuities for verification claims.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses arguments, loads the target .wpilog file, and dispatches to entry-summary, grep-filter, dump, or pose-jump-analysis output modes.

nodes.name: Entry
nodes.summary: Lightweight record representing a single WPILOG entry (id, name, type, metadata, and accumulated decoded records) used as the core data structure throughout parsing.

nodes.name: run_headless_sim.py
nodes.summary: Headless launch-check script that runs `gradlew simulateJava -Pheadless=true`, watches stdout for the robot-program-starting marker and a settle window, then kills the process tree and reports pass/fail — proving the build compiles and every subsystem singleton constructs without exercising command/state-machine behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicitly documents the limits of what a passing run proves (init-only, no scheduler/commands) to prevent overclaiming behavior verification from this gate alone.

nodes.name: kill_tree

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: launches the headless sim subprocess, streams its output on a background thread while scanning for error/success markers and the init marker, enforces a settle window and overall timeout, then reports pass/fail and optionally lists/parses produced logs.

nodes.summary: Wraps a CTRE HootAutoReplay instance bound to boolean and double signal accessors, exposing isReplay()/update() for driving replayed hub-active and shot-timer state.

nodes.name: LimelightHelpers
nodes.summary: Static utility class exposing the full Limelight NetworkTables API surface — pose estimation, raw target/fiducial/detection data, IMU data, and pipeline/LED/crop/orientation configuration — for every camera named in the deploy.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Pulls the latest MegaTag2 pose estimate and validity/timestamp/tag-count data from the Limelight and writes it into the VisionIOInputs each periodic loop.

nodes.name: getPoseResetEstimate
nodes.summary: Returns an optional MegaTag1 pose estimate used to seed/reset the drivetrain's pose estimator when a fresh, valid Limelight reading is available.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a simulated vision pose-estimate input directly from the ground-truth pose supplier, timestamping it with the FPGA clock for both estimate slots.

nodes.name: telemeterize
nodes.summary: Per-loop telemetry callback that publishes drivetrain pose, chassis speeds, module states/targets/positions, and odometry timing to NetworkTables, SignalLogger, and AdvantageKit's Logger.

nodes.name: toPose3D
nodes.summary: Converts a raw Limelight double array (translation + quaternion) into a WPILib Pose3d, guarding against malformed/short arrays.

nodes.name: toPose2D
nodes.summary: Converts a raw Limelight double array into a WPILib Pose2d by extracting the planar translation and yaw component.

nodes.name: pose3dToArray
nodes.summary: Flattens a Pose3d back into the Limelight double-array wire format (translation + quaternion) for outgoing NetworkTables writes.

nodes.name: pose2dToArray
nodes.summary: Flattens a Pose2d back into the Limelight double-array wire format for outgoing NetworkTables writes.

nodes.name: getBotPoseEstimate
nodes.summary: Internal helper that reads a named botpose NetworkTables entry (MegaTag1 or MegaTag2 variant), parses timing/tag-count/latency metadata, and assembles a PoseEstimate record.

nodes.name: getRawFiducials
nodes.summary: Parses the raw AprilTag fiducial array from NetworkTables into RawFiducial records (ID, tx/ty, area, distances, ambiguity).

nodes.name: getRawDetections
nodes.summary: Parses the raw neural-detector output array from NetworkTables into RawDetection records (class ID, corner coordinates, confidence).

nodes.name: getRawTargets
nodes.summary: Parses the raw retroreflective/color target array from NetworkTables into RawTarget records.

nodes.name: printPoseEstimate
nodes.summary: Debug helper that pretty-prints a PoseEstimate's pose, timestamp, latency, tag count, and per-tag fiducial details to stdout.

nodes.name: SetFiducialDownscalingOverride
nodes.summary: Sets the AprilTag pipeline's image downscale factor override (auto or a fixed 1x-4x factor) on a named Limelight.

nodes.name: setCameraPose_RobotSpace
nodes.summary: Writes the camera's mounting pose relative to robot center (forward/side/up offsets and roll/pitch/yaw) to the Limelight's NetworkTables config entry.

nodes.name: getLatestResults
nodes.summary: Fetches and deserializes the full JSON results dump from a Limelight into a LimelightResults object (including IMU data), logging parse time and reporting errors on failure.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: This is Team 4935's 2026 FRC robot codebase, built on WPILib/GradleRIO with a CI badge and two Desmos calculators linked for external design reference. The README itself is intentionally minimal -- the real architectural story lives in the code and in docs/claudex, which this tour will walk you through step by step, ending with those deeper documents once you have the context to appreciate them.

tour.title: Robot Bootstrap
tour.description: Main.java is the standard WPILib entry point -- it does almost nothing itself, just handing control to RobotBase.startRobot with a Robot supplier. Robot.java is where the real bootstrap happens: it extends AdvantageKit's LoggedRobot, wires up logging receivers differently for REAL/SIM/REPLAY modes, owns the Vision and HubActiveState singletons, and drives the WPILib command scheduler every cycle. Everything else in this tour is reachable from what Robot.java sets up here.
tour.languageLesson: Main.java uses a Java method reference (Robot::new) so WPILib's RobotBase can construct your robot class lazily. AdvantageKit's REAL/SIM/REPLAY branching in Robot.java is a common WPILib pattern for keeping one codebase runnable on hardware, in simulation, and against recorded logs.

tour.title: RobotContainer: Wiring the Robot
tour.description: RobotContainer.java is the highest fan-out file in the codebase -- it constructs and wires together every singleton subsystem (drivetrain, intake, shooter, vision, superstructure), registers PathPlanner autonomous commands, and hands off to OperatorControls to bind joystick and control-box inputs. Think of this as the assembly diagram: once you've read this file, you know which subsystems exist and how they're connected before diving into any one of them.

tour.title: Shared Constants & Field Data
tour.description: Constants.java is the single most depended-upon file in the project (highest fan-in) -- it centralizes CAN IDs, vision tuning, and the physical/simulation placeholders that every subsystem's IOReal/IOSim implementation reads from. FieldConstants.java and POI.java layer field geometry and named, alliance-mirrored Points of Interest on top, feeding the drivetrain's auto-align commands you'll see in Step 8.

tour.title: Intake: The IO-Isolation Pattern
tour.description: This is the pattern every subsystem in the codebase follows, so it's worth understanding fully here: Intake.java holds hardware-agnostic business logic (roller/pivot control plus jam-detection and eject-pulse recovery), IntakeIO.java is the interface that logic programs against, and IntakeIOReal.java / IntakeIOSim.java are swappable implementations -- one driving real TalonFX hardware via CTRE Phoenix 6, the other using pure WPILib physics (SingleJointedArmSim, DCMotorSim) plus maple-sim for game-piece pickup. Per CLAUDE.md's hardware-isolation rule, vendor APIs are confined entirely to the IOReal file.
tour.languageLesson: This is dependency inversion in Java: the logic class (Intake) depends only on an interface (IntakeIO), never on a concrete implementation. Which implementation gets injected -- IntakeIOReal or IntakeIOSim -- is decided once, at construction time in RobotContainer, letting the exact same subsystem logic run unmodified on hardware or in simulation.

tour.title: Shooter: The Same Pattern, Reinforced
tour.description: Shooter.java repeats the exact IO-isolation structure from Step 5 -- logic class, IO interface, IOReal, IOSim -- but with different mechanisms: flywheel RPM, agitator, and indexer motors, plus its own jam-clearing routine (indexJam()). ShooterIOReal is notable because it drives a mixed motor ecosystem (TalonFX flywheels/indexer, a NEO 550 agitator on a TalonFXS), showing the pattern still holds even when the hardware underneath isn't uniform.

tour.title: Superstructure: The Centralized State Machine
tour.description: Superstructure.java is where Intake, Shooter, and Vision from the last three steps get coordinated -- not through composed Commands, but through a 254-style centralized state machine: a SuperstructureState enum (OFF/INTAKING/EJECTING/STOWED/ALIGNING/SHOOTING) with all arbitration logic living directly in periodic()'s switch-case. HubActiveState.java feeds it match-timing context (whether the scoring hub is active), rounding out the state machine's inputs.
tour.languageLesson: Centralizing arbitration in one periodic() switch-case (rather than spreading it across composed Command classes) makes the full set of legal state transitions readable in one place -- a deliberate tradeoff favoring explicitness over WPILib's usual command-composition idiom.

tour.title: Swerve Drivetrain: The Sanctioned Exception
tour.description: CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java is CTRE Tuner X-generated code, and per CLAUDE.md it's the one subsystem explicitly exempted from hardware isolation -- it's extended in place with SysId routines, PathPlanner integration, vision-fused pose estimation, and the POI auto-align commands from Step 4. TunerConstants.java supplies its generated gains/CAN IDs/module geometry, while MapleSimSwerveDrivetrain.java is the maple-sim physics wrapper CommandSwerveDrivetrain delegates to for its simulation thread. This cluster has the highest mutual connectivity in the whole codebase, which is why it's grouped as one step.

tour.title: Vision: AprilTags and Pose Fusion
tour.description: Vision.java estimates hub/pass target positions from AprilTag geometry, fuses camera pose estimates into the drivetrain's odometry (Step 8), and computes shooter RPM from a distance lookup table -- it's the second-highest fan-in file in the project. VisionIOReal.java talks to real Limelight cameras through the vendored LimelightHelpers.java (about 99 static NetworkTables methods) for MegaTag2 pose estimates, while VisionIOSim.java fabricates pose estimates directly from ground truth, keeping headless simulation hardware-free.

tour.title: Autonomous Routines & Path Data
tour.description: Autonomous behavior in this project isn't hardcoded Java -- it's authored visually in PathPlanner and deployed as JSON-like data files that CommandSwerveDrivetrain and RobotContainer load at runtime. An .auto file like 'LT Neutral' sequences named path segments (such as Depot.path) into a full autonomous routine, while navgrid.json defines the obstacle grid PathPlanner's on-the-fly replanning avoids. This is the same POI/FieldConstants geometry from Step 4, expressed as data instead of code.

tour.title: Behavior Tests
tour.description: These JUnit tests boot a real Robot instance on a background thread under HAL simulation and drive it through actual state transitions rather than mocking them -- RobotLifecycleTest checks Vision's IMU mode transitions on entering autonomous, SuperstructureEjectingTest verifies the EJECTING state (Step 7) drives the right motor outputs and cleanly cancels back to STOWED, and IntakeJamRecoveryTest proves the jam-recovery pulse from Step 5's Intake.setRoller() actually fires and auto-resumes. This is gate 2.5 of the project's verification loop -- proof of command/state-machine behavior, not just compilation.

tour.title: Build, CI, and Verification Tooling
tour.description: build.gradle configures GradleRIO, the Java 17 toolchain, RoboRIO deploy targets, and the vendor/JUnit 5 dependencies used throughout this tour. The GitHub Actions workflow (main.yml) runs a full build and test on every push inside the WPILib roboRIO cross-compilation container -- the automated form of gates 1 and 2.5. The two SKILLS scripts are the manual/agent-facing equivalents: run_headless_sim.py launches gradlew simulateJava headlessly and confirms the robot program actually starts, while parse_akit_log.py decodes recorded .wpilog files to catch pose-jump regressions after the fact.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows trigger on 'on:' events (push/pull_request here), run 'jobs' that can parallelize, and execute 'steps' sequentially within each job -- this workflow's single job builds inside a pinned WPILib Docker image so CI matches the exact roboRIO cross-compilation toolchain developers use locally.

tour.title: Architecture Rationale & History
tour.description: Now that you've seen the hardware-isolation pattern, the Superstructure state machine, and the sanctioned swerve exception in practice, docs/claudex/architecture.md explains the *why* behind each of those CLAUDE.md rules. docs/claudex/verification-loop.md defines the gate system you saw enforced in Steps 11-12, and docs/claudex/history.md is the append-only changelog of every refactor pass that got this codebase to its current state -- the deepest layer of context for anyone continuing this work.
